guard: a hosted run verb refuses an unanswered manager describe against the rail it rode, and offers --local only where nothing else could have answered
why: The single sentence this replaces was measured in #1630 against a manager that was running the
whole time. Its two halves fail differently. The question sends an operator to hunt a process
that is up, which costs time. `--local` drives the run in the calling process and names the
caller as its answerer, so an operator who follows the tool's own advice submits a run answer
under the wrong identity; the seat on that mesh declined and left its answer unsubmitted.
The mutation restores the pre-fix sentence for every rail, which is the exact regression, and
the cell that catches it asserts on both halves rather than on the headline alone.

mutations.name: the refusal returns to one rail-blind sentence, with the question and the --local remedy on every rail
mutations.replace: return `no manager answered on the endpoint rails (${detail}); is a manager running for this mesh? A run can still be driven from this terminal with --local`;
mutations.expectRed: versioned rail: neither the false question nor the --local remedy that follows from it is printed
